questions.q: What were the people to offer to Yahweh when they divided the land as an inheritance?
questions.a: The people were to set apart a specific portion of land as a holy gift to Yahweh.

questions.q: How much pastureland was to be around the temple?
questions.a: There was to be an open space 27 meters wide surrounding that plot on every side.

questions.q: What was to be in the section that was 25,000 long and 10,000 wide?
questions.a: The sanctuary, the holy of holies, was to be in that section.

questions.q: The holy part of the land would be a place for what?
questions.a: The holy part of the land would be a place for the houses of the priests and for the sanctuary.

questions.q: To whom would the area of the city belong?
questions.a: The area of the city would belong to all the house of Israel.

questions.q: Whose land would be on both sides of the holy part of the land and the city?
questions.a: The land of the prince would be on both sides of the holy part of the land and the city.

questions.q: What would the princes of Israel no longer do to Yahweh’s people?
questions.a: The princes of Israel would no longer mistreat Yahweh’s people.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the princes of Israel to stop doing?
questions.a: Yahweh tells the princes of Israel to remove violence and destruction and to stop evicting his people.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say must be made accurate?
questions.a: Yahweh says the scales, ephahs, and baths must be accurate.

questions.q: What part of a homer were the ephah and the bath each to carry?
questions.a: The ephah and the bath were each to carry a tenth of a homer.

questions.q: How many gerahs make a shekel?
questions.a: A shekel is 20 gerahs.

questions.q: What part of the wheat and the barley were the people to give as an offering?
questions.a: The people were to give a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.

questions.q: How much oil from ten baths would be the regulation offering of oil?
questions.a: A tenth of a bath for every ten baths would be the regulation offering of oil.

questions.q: How many sheep were to be given from every 200 sheep in the flock?
questions.a: One sheep from every 200 sheep in the flock was to be given for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.

questions.q: To whom would the people of the land give their contributions?
questions.a: The people of the land would give their contributions to the prince in Israel.

questions.q: Who would be responsible for providing the offerings at the festivals, the new moons, and the Sabbaths of the house of Israel?
questions.a: The prince in Israel would be responsible for providing the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the drink offering at those times.

questions.q: When were the people to take a bull with no defects to purify the sanctuary?
questions.a: They were to take a bull with no defects on the first day of the first month.

questions.q: Where was the priest to put the blood of the sin offering?
questions.a: The priest was to put the blood on the doorpost of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorpost of the gate of the inner courtyard.

questions.q: When were the people to make atonement for the house on behalf of anyone who sinned without intending to or without knowing?
questions.a: They were to make atonement for the house on the seventh day of the month.

questions.q: When would there be a seven-day festival of unleavened bread?
questions.a: On the fourteenth day of the first month there would be the Passover, a seven-day festival when the people eat unleavened bread.

questions.q: Who was to provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land?
questions.a: The prince was to provide the bull as a sin offering.

questions.q: How many bulls and rams was the prince to provide as a burnt offering each day of the seven-day festival?
questions.a: The prince was to provide seven bulls and seven rams with no defects each day, and also a male goat as a sin offering each day.

questions.q: How much grain offering was the prince to make for each bull and each ram?
questions.a: The prince was to make a grain offering of an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of oil for each ephah.

questions.q: What offerings were to be given on the fifteenth day of the seventh month?
questions.a: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and offerings of oil were to be given as at the Passover festival.

commentary.text: In the period here foretold, the worship and the ministers of God will be provided for; the princes will rule with justice, as holding their power under Christ; the people will live in peace, ease, and godliness. These things seem to be represented in language taken from the customs of the times in which the prophet wrote. Christ is our Passover that is sacrificed for us: we celebrate the memorial of that sacrifice, and feast upon it, triumphing in our deliverance out of the Egyptian slavery of sin, and our preservation from the destroying sword of Divine justice, in the Lord's supper, which is our passover feast; as the whole Christian life is, and must be, the feast of the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
